title: Decision Junction — Visible Route
prompt:
Edit the first referenced mobile UI comp, preserving its approved Nudge airport-wayfinding visual world and its strong focus. Produce one polished high-fidelity portrait phone screen at 9:16, showing the active Performance state for an adaptive workout.

Keep these core elements from the first image: white Nudge header, black route band reading PLAN / PERFORMANCE / COOLDOWN / REVIEW with PERFORMANCE highlighted in airport yellow; dominant current-exercise composition with “02 SHOULDER PRESS”, set context, weight and reps controls; an exceptionally large, unmistakable airport-yellow “START SET” action panel with a bold right arrow that is easy to hit while handling weights; black rest band; and a clear next-decision card saying “Shoulder press is ready” with agency-preserving choices “GO NEXT” and “STAY HERE”.

Resolve alternate exercise navigation without weakening the main action. Replace the vague bottom “WORKOUT OVERVIEW” control with a subordinate but obvious section titled “YOUR ROUTE · 2 OF 4”. Show three compact, full-width, tappable route rows below it: “01 GOBLET SQUAT · 3/3 SETS” marked DONE, “03 ONE-ARM ROW · 0/3 SETS” marked READY, and “04 DEAD BUG · 0/2 SETS” marked READY. Each row should have a large enough tap target, a bold two-digit wayfinding identifier, plain status text, and a restrained chevron. Keep the route section visually quieter than START SET and the next-decision card: white or very pale concrete rows, thin graphite rules, black typography, tiny yellow status accents only. Let the first route row peek into the initial viewport so discoverability is obvious, with remaining rows naturally available by scrolling. Do not use a small “change exercise” button, dropdown, hamburger, modal, floating action, trophy, checkered flag, streak, celebration, urgency language, or decorative illustration.

The hierarchy must read instantly: 1) start this set, 2) expected next exercise decision, 3) choose a different exercise from the route. Use saturated airport yellow, jet black, signal white, pale concrete, graphite; humanist transport-signage sans; oversized identifiers; bold arrows; strict rectangular geometry; generous spacing; no gradients, shadows, rounded cards, or excessive borders. Ensure all text is legible and plausible, all controls look tappable, and the lower route area feels integrated rather than bolted on.
